description: Part single, part 2-storey front, side, rear extensions, involving relocation of existing garage, 2x rear dormers and a front facing balcony.
decision_conditions: Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of all retained trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP). The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures.Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:1.	location and detailed installation methodology of all utility services/drainage systems in close proximity to Root Protection Areas (RPAs) (avoiding the RPAs of all retained trees) (RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012);2.	timings and methods of removal of any existing hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs, and how these areas shall be protected between removal of existing and installation of approved;3.	details of any construction that necessitates level changes within RPAs;4.	a detailed methodology for the installation of foundations within RPAs, following the specification approved under discharge of Condition 5 (foundations);5.	a full specification for the construction of all paths, parking areas and driveways (including alterations to the existing layout of internal hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;6.	detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;7.	a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;8.	a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all trees during both demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the fencing and extent of ground protection;9.	a specification for scaffolding and ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary);10.	details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;This condition shall not be discharged until Condition 5  has first been approved and discharged.The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 and 81, 81 pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 and the British Standard for Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction (BS 5837:2012).

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:0106 Rev CTPP-01 Rev A02A03A04A05B0708BS5837 Arboricultural Method StatementReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture as specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

The glazing serving the additional side windows at first floor, as seen along the proposed flank elevations of the development indicated on drawing No. 04A, shall be in obscured glass with an equivalent obscuration as level 3 on the Pilkington Obscuration Range and the window shall be non-opening unless the parts of the window which can be opened are more than 1.7 metres above the floor of the room in which the window is installed. The glazing shall not be altered without the approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of adjoining and neighbouring properties

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a full specification for the foundations shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The specification shall demonstrate adherence to the guidelines set out in NHBC Chapter 4.2 Building near Trees.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the development will be adequately constructed against a risk of future subsidence and to ensure that off site trees of high amenity value and public benefit / protected trees will not be at risk through implication in possible future subsidence cases, in accordance with Policy DMD80(b) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including any ground clearance, tree works, demolition or construction), details of all tree protection monitoring and site supervision by a suitably qualified tree specialist (where arboricultural expertise is required) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: Required prior to the commencement of development in order that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during development works and to ensure that, as far as is possible, the work is carried out in accordance with the approved details pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 in accordance 1990 with Policy DMD80 Policy G7, 81 pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 and the British Standard for Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction (BS 5837:2012).

The completed schedule of site supervision and monitoring of the arboricultural protection measures as approved in condition (7) shall be submitted for approval in writing by the Local Planning Authority within 28 days from completion of the development hereby permitted. This condition may only be fully discharged on completion of the development, subject to satisfactory written evidence of compliance through contemporaneous supervision and monitoring of the tree protection throughout construction by a suitably qualified and pre-appointed tree specialist.Reason: In order to ensure compliance with the tree protection and arboricultural supervision details submitted under condition (6 & 7) pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 in accordance with Policy DMD80 of the Development Management Plan and Policy G7 The London Plan
